I've been farming these 4.1 mu for fifty years, just me and my wife now that the children have their own lives in the city. My wheat went into the ground last October after the National Day holiday, same as every year. I bought improved seed from the county co-op — not the most expensive kind, but the one I've used for years and I trust it. Before planting, I rotary tilled the field and put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base. Now that it's warming up and the wheat is greening up, I'll topdress with urea once the weather settles — about 40 jin per mu. I learned my lesson three years ago when I tried to save money on fertilizer and the wheat turned yellow at jointing, and I lost nearly 200 jin per mu. Never again. I'll irrigate three times from the well: once now at green-up, once at jointing around Qingming, and once at grain filling if the rain doesn't come. The electricity for pumping isn't cheap, but dry wheat means empty bins, so I don't skip water. I'll spray herbicide once, and keep an eye out for rust — if I see spots on the leaves, I'll spray fungicide too.

For the maize, as soon as the wheat comes off the thresher in early June, I have to move fast — the window is only a few days before the soil dries out. Everyone plants hybrid maize now; you can't save your own seed and expect a decent crop. I won't do much tillage, just plant directly or maybe a light rotary pass, because there's no time between wheat harvest and maize planting. I'll put compound fertilizer down with the seed and topdress once with urea when the maize is knee-high. I'll irrigate twice if the summer drought hits, usually at the big trumpet stage and then at grain filling. Two sprays should be enough — herbicide right after planting, and insecticide if the corn borer shows up. I expect about 840 jin per mu from the wheat and 920 jin from the maize, about the same as last year if the weather holds. My neighbor Wang got a little more, but he's younger and has a bigger machine, so I don't compare too much. With just the two of us, we do what we can and thank heaven for the rest.
